While it still omits broader legal, societal, and structural dimensions, it does not contain the factual mischaracterization found in response a (e.g., treating outcome favorability as a type of justice) and includes more contextual elements beyond a simple listing of the three justice types. coverage_deep.explantion: Both responses suffer from the same set of deep‑coverage shortcomings: they provide only superficial definitions of distributive, procedural, and interactional justice, offer no concrete workplace examples, and fail to explain the psychological or behavioral mechanisms linking justice perceptions to outcomes. Neither answer supplies richer detail or illustrative cases that would give one a clear advantage over the other. Consequently, the appropriate adjudication is a tie.
